slides.title: GateLite: Sparse Gated Adapters for Low-Resource Speech Recognition
subtitle: A. Example and B. Sample
Synthetic example paper - interface demo only
slides.notes: Introduce the problem in one sentence: adapting big speech encoders when a language has only a few hours of data.

slides.title: Full fine-tuning overfits when a language has under 10 h of labelled speech

bullets.text: Encoders are pre-trained on high-resource data, then adapted per language
A 300M-parameter encoder overfits with only a few hours of transcribed speech
Dense adapters spend capacity on every frame, even the easy ones

slides.notes: Stress the data regime: under 10 hours. Ask the audience how many of their languages fall below that.
slides.transition: So the question is how to adapt cheaply without overfitting.

slides.title: GateLite routes each frame to 2 of 8 small adapter experts
bullets: Sparse gated adapter: **2 of 8** experts active per frame
Load-balancing regulariser keeps expert usage uniform
Evaluated on five languages with 1 to 50 h of training data
slides.notes: These are the three contributions as the paper states them; the next slide shows the block.
